title: research: consume encoded twiddle headers on signed packet tapes
body:
PR3593 emits an encoded twiddle header, while the preceding signed-packet adapter takes host exponent tuples. This package closes that single-header interface: a new sequential consumer directly borrows the producer's actual header and descriptor tapes and applies the exact signed polynomial rotation to a complete Gaussian packet.

Initialization follows encoded extents; marked-top countdowns avoid a full counter-width scan per coefficient. The source-bound proof gives a consumer tariff at most `256*(2*r*w+ell+w+1)`, six owned tapes and a 34-role producer/consumer join with shared header/descriptor storage counted once. Borrowed data and heads are restored, and private work is erased on success and signed-minimum rejection. Producer correctness remains an explicit retained premise.

Validation: both registered CPython 3.12.15 commands, including isolation, optimization and warnings-as-errors; 56 all-residue packets, eight signed-word cases, 83 countdown cases, four actual producer joins with opposite round trips, eight controls, and independent operation-counter reconciliation. The joined examples with ell=8, K=4, h=5, r=256 and w=10 emit residues 264/248 and 424/88, use 21,537 cells each and retain exact tariffs. Three frozen producer files match original Git bytes; metadata and committed-byte/source-history checks pass.

Review replaced host-sized initialization loops with encoded scans and added borrowed/private alias rejection. No host-decoded header controls consumer execution. Constructor allocation/admission, executable ell limits, signed representability and valid-framing premises are explicit.

Scope: one independent borrowed address and one complete signed packet. No address enumeration, reusable consumer object, arbitrary malformed-input recovery, complete synthetic round, normalized root/layer, supplier admission or selected-frontier change. The full caller invoice remains open.

Package: `research/encoded-twiddle-packet-consumer`. Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2612#discussioncomment-19014835

Credit Nick Petalas's PR3593 and packet/header lineage, Philipp, Jose Manuel, Douglas Colkitt and retained synthetic-transform sources. Prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate same-session implementation/proof/verification agents; not independent human acceptance or formal kernel verification.
